summary: Plan PQC migration with FIPS 203, 204 and 205, cryptographic inventories and crypto-agile design. Explore the course and build your roadmap.
lede: Post-quantum cryptography uses algorithms designed to resist quantum-computer attacks, while crypto-agility helps systems adapt as cryptographic needs change. For CISOs, cybersecurity architects, and IT security teams, this course covers mapping cryptographic dependencies, assessing harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure, and prioritizing staged migration plans. Exercises produce an asset inventory, prioritization scorecard, architecture map, and roadmap for internal review.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess cryptographic exposure, govern security architecture, or plan technology change affecting sensitive data. It suits roles that need to scope PQC migration and communicate priorities across security, technology, and procurement teams.
prerequisites: Prior experience in cybersecurity, IT security, cryptography, security architecture, or technology risk is recommended. Familiarity with public-key cryptography and enterprise IT systems will help you apply the exercises. Coding is not required; algorithm engineering and production deployment are outside the hands-on scope.
